title: frames/1 — a frame set's frames.json sidecar
description: Written next to equal-canvas PNG frames by sheet_to_frames.py, breathe.py and video_loop.py; read by audit_frames.py, audit_pixel.py, frames_to_anim.py, registry_ingest.py and the Unity importer and audit. Producers add their own keys freely at the top level; the keys below are the contract.

tool.description: the script that wrote this file, e.g. sheet_to_frames.py

source.description: what the frames came from: a path (breathe.py) or {file, sha256, fps} (video_loop.py). sheet_to_frames.py writes `sheet` instead.

canvas.description: [W, H] in px; every frame file is exactly this size

pivot.description: the coarse statement of the pivot, kept for older readers; pivot_norm is authoritative

pivot_norm.description: [x, y], a fraction of the canvas from its bottom-left: where the sprite's pivot goes. Unity's spritePivot uses the same convention, so it is written as is with SpriteAlignment.Custom.

key_color.description: the declared chroma key the frames were keyed against, lowercase #rrggbb (sheet_to_frames --key-color/--bg-color, video_frames' key.declared). null only when the producer was told explicitly that the art was never chroma-keyed (native alpha); a reader then skips the fringe measurement and says so.

key_painted.description: optional: the key colour actually found on the generated image's border, lowercase #rrggbb

loop.description: true: the clip loops (loopTime). Always written: a typed reader cannot tell an absent bool from false.

hold_last.description: true: a one-shot that ends on, and holds, its last pose (not a frame count)

register.description: how the frames were seated on the canvas. Flat: no object-valued member, so a pattern-based reader that takes the register body as {...} cannot lose fields.

reference_core_height_px.description: the drawn character height the set is normalised to: the reference frame's core height, in px of the written frame files (after any pixel upscale). Every set of one character carries the same number; import PPU = this / the character's height in world units.

foot_margin_px.description: transparent px between the reference frame's feet line and the canvas bottom (0 for a centroid set)

verdict.description: the producer's own gate over the set. Not a gate/1 report: it keeps {ok, faults}.

pixel.description: present only for a pixel-art set (sheet_to_frames --pixelate / --pixel-snap)

block_px.description: F: written file px per art pixel (the --upscale factor)
